author: Codex documentation author
frontend: Committed conversations lab at port 43302 for every guide step; Mailpit at port 48427 for the Portal sign-ins and the resolution email check; the lab API for the second legal session's competing writes, one later Document Version per converted record, and state reads
browser: Playwright 1.62.1 Chromium from the private documentation cache, headless, one isolated context per identity; scripts written by the reviewer from the guide text
fixturePreparation: Reused the author's request types, Fields, Contract and Matter types, and Matter templates by identifier. Created two Entities of its own (Independent old Entity and Independent live Entity), created twenty fresh fictional Requests R-108 to R-127 as Jonas Weber through the Portal API (ten per staff role: triage, resolve, race, contract, matter, re-target, deferred, archived, bad template, conversion race) with two distinct PDFs each, then archived the old Entity. The contract and matter Requests carry a reference to the old Entity set while it was live; the Portal has no Entity picker.

Requests decided by earlier reviewer runs were replaced by fresh copies before the final runs: R-128 and R-129 for the Administrator's resolve steps and R-130 for the Administrator's contract conversion. The final records name the Requests they used.

Comments at all three tiers with paper were posted through the Inbox Comments panel as the acting role before each main conversion. Competing decisions were made by the other staff role through the API while the browser's write was held, so the dialog met a real conflict. The people-load and save failures used controlled browser responses; the successful retries wrote through the app.

One later Document Version was uploaded through the API to the first promoted Document on each of C-59, M-39, C-63 and M-42 to check that the Requester's original downloads did not change. DOC-017 owns that guide; this is not acceptance of it.

Fictional records created by the final runs: Administrator C-59, M-39, M-40 (re-target), C-60 (deferred), C-61 (archived type), M-41 (No template after the refused default), C-62 (won by Nadia Haddad); Legal Team Member C-63, M-42, M-43, C-64, C-65, M-44, C-66 (won by Daniel Okafor). Earlier reviewer runs left C-58 and unused fresh Requests in this disposable lab.
corrections: None from the walkthrough. The three conversion-guide sentences changed by this seat's earlier source check (commit 4a540b8c) were followed as written: the Template control appeared as soon as a Matter type was set, and the refused template default was recovered by Cancel, reopen, No template and a typed required answer.
observations: Six earlier steps failed on reviewer harness locators, not on app or guide behaviour: an alert whose text sits beside a Retry button, the retained assignee rendered inside a span that also carries the avatar initials, a list-row control already reading Reassign after a prior run, the dialog's single "Priority High" line, and a GET on a Document versions route that does not exist. Each was corrected in the harness and the run repeated on unchanged guide bytes; the failed steps are retained above with their run tag.
The retained assignee is visible on a decided Request immediately after resolution, before any reload; the earlier failure was the locator.
The resolution note also reached Jonas by email from the lab (subject "Your request is resolved: R-N · …"); external delivery is not claimed.

The stale template default was refused by the API with "<Field>: pick one of the options." while the dialog showed no box for that optional Field, which is the case the guide's second refusal paragraph describes.
Converts to reads the bare module ("Contract") for a module-only request type and for one whose configured type was archived; the dialog then offers the live type picker as the guide says.
A Contract created by conversion has no Owner and a Matter no Matter Manager (both read null); the Contract team read route is POST-only, so ownership was checked on the record itself.
